claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT) on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission marked the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years.
The Artemis II crew consisted of four persons.
The Artemis II crew completed a roughly 10-day, 695,081-mile journey around the Moon.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred in the Pacific Ocean approximately 60 miles off the coast of San Diego.
Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen were reported to be in good health.
The Navy dive team secured the Orion capsule "Integrity".
As discussed on Reddit, the Navy dive team assisted the Artemis II crew.
The Artemis II crew transferred to the USS John P. Murtha for immediate health checks.
The Orion spacecraft completed the fiery re-entry, including a 6-minute communications blackout, as reported by the BBC.
The Artemis II mission marked the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft.
